`Account`, `ServiceAccount` and `SelfHostedSync` are built from smaller pieces, all exported. Use them when
you need control the high-level classes don't give, for example your own storage of sync state, or the
sync loop over files that aren't vaults.

### Sync loop {#sync-loop}

The sync loop is the shared Rust core's (ov-sync): `vault.sync()` on an account vault, `syncDatabase` on a
self-hosted server, or `account.core.syncVaultKdbx(vaultId, bytes, base)` for an account vault you hold as a
file. Each does a `HEAD` when nothing changed locally (`vault.sync({ localChanged: false })`,
`syncDatabase(id, bytes, credentials, { localChanged: false })`), a download, the rollback checks (revision and the sync
generation inside the file), the three-way merge against the base copy kept in the offline cache, the
`If-Match` upload, and on `412` download, merge and retry (up to five times, then `too_many_conflicts`).
Since 1.0 there is no `syncKdbx`; see [Migrating to 1.0](/docs/sdk/migrating-to-1.0/).

`report.clockOffsetMs` is how far this computer's clock is ahead of the sync server's (negative: behind),
from the server's `Date` header; it is undefined when the server sent none the client could read (a browser
needs the server to list `Date` in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`). Sync decides edits and deletions against
the base copy, not by clocks, but a wrong clock still stamps entries with wrong times and breaks TOTP codes, so
warn when `isClockSkewed(report.clockOffsetMs)` (off by more than `CLOCK_SKEW_WARNING_MS`, 5 minutes), as the
desktop and iOS apps do.

### Merge {#merge}

`mergeDatabases(local, remote, base)` is the merge on its own, on `Kdbx` handles (`openKdbx(bytes, key)`), and
`kdbxMerge(local, remote, base, key)` the same on file bytes; see [Merge behaviour](/docs/sdk/merge-behaviour/). Like
the desktop app, it applies permanent deletions only with the base: an item deleted on one side goes from
both unless the other side changed it since the base. Deleting to the Recycle Bin is a move and syncs
normally.

### HTTP clients {#http-clients}

- `AuthClient` has a method for every account server route. `account.auth` is one signed in with the
  account's session: it borrows the core's access token (the core refreshes it). `TokenManager` is for an
  `AuthClient` you run without an `Account`.
- `SyncClient` covers every sync server route: `vault(id)` and `database(id)` return blob handles with
  `get`, `head`, `put`, `delete`, `history` and `getRevision`, and `subscribeEvents` opens the events stream.

Every client takes `fetch` (any `fetch`-compatible function, default `globalThis.fetch`) and `headers` to add
to every request, such as a `User-Agent` in Node.

### Vaults and KDBX {#vaults-and-kdbx}

A database is the core's `Vault` handle: `openLocalVault(bytes, credentials)`, `createLocalVault(name,
credentials)`, `vault.saveLocal()`, and the entry, group, field, history and attachment methods on it.
`credentials` are `{ password?, keyFile? }` as bytes; `passwordCredentials(password)` and
`vaultCredentials(vaultKey)` make them. The web app's plain-data helpers work on a `Vault`:
`decryptKdbx`, `createNewKdbx`, `collectAllDbData`, `addEntryToDb`, `editEntryInDb` (history first),
`deleteEntryFromDb`, group helpers and `exportSelectedGroupsToKdbx`. For references and items:
`parseReference`, `readField`, `writeField`, `findEntry`, `parseItemReference`, `itemOf`, `listItems` and
`setItemFields`. Entry and group ids are 32 lowercase hex digits.

The lower-level file handle is `Kdbx` (`openKdbx`, `createVaultKdbx`, `openWithKeyVersions`, `saveKdbx`,
`rekeyToVaultKey`, `merge`, `importFrom`, `snapshot`, …), which `@openvireo/sdk/merge` works with.

### Argon2 {#argon2}

Argon2 (all three types, any output length) runs on the core's lite module. At m = 64 MiB, t = 3 it takes
about 110 ms (Node 24, M-series Mac), as fast as the hash-wasm build 0.x used. `setArgon2Impl(fn)` replaces it for the AUK
(for example with a native binding in Node); `coreArgon2` is the default.

### The core modules {#the-core-modules}

The SDK calls `@openvireo/core-wasm`, openvireo-core compiled to WebAssembly, in two modules: the **lite** one
(primitives, share links, TOTP; about 190 KB gzip) and the **full** one (everything else, about 880 KB
gzip). Both load synchronously the first time they're needed. In a browser, `await ready()` once at startup
so the full module compiles before the first synchronous call. `@openvireo/sdk/share` loads only the lite
module, so a public share page stays small. OPAQUE is in the full module (opaque-ke 4.0.1, the same suite as
the account server and the desktop app).
